jobs.title: Product Owner, Xsolla Partner Network
jobs.description: About You We are looking for a Product Owner to join the team behind Xsolla Partner Network (XPN). The role is based in the US, and we’re open to strong candidates globally. Partner Network connects game publishers with content creators to drive discovery, engagement, and revenue. XPN is a two-sided marketplace. We help publishers run creator marketing campaigns (xsolla.com/partner-network), and we give creators a way to join those campaigns, along with tools to manage and grow their channels (xsolla.com/for/creators). Each side has its own users and goals, and each shapes the other. Helping both sides succeed together is what makes this role so interesting. You’ll work closely with customers on both sides and with a collaborative team that’s building something new in the creator economy. You’ll bring what you learn back to the Product Director and the team, help shape where the product goes, and then work alongside design and engineering to bring it to life. This is a hands-on role that mixes customer conversations, product definition, and day-to-day delivery. If you enjoy turning what you learn from customers into shipped features, and you like doing it with a team that moves fast and supports each other, we’d love to meet you. About Us Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game. For more information, visit xsolla.com. Responsibilities: Research and discovery. Get to know both sides of the XPN marketplace: the game publishers running creator campaigns and the creators bringing those campaigns to life. Talk with customers, gather insights, and keep up with trends in the creator economy and gaming. What you learn shapes where the product goes next. Coordinate the roadmap. jobs.description: About Tratta Tratta is the platform that powers credit and collections at scale, and we try to make it enjoyable to work on. Our clients are collection agencies and law firms recovering debt from consumers. Their account data lands in Tratta and is mapped and validated on the way in. They run email and SMS campaigns off it. Consumers land on a payment portal carrying the client's brand, where they can pay, negotiate a plan or sign an agreement electronically without ever speaking to a collector. Payments clear through us by card, ACH or check, and it all feeds back into reporting that shapes the next campaign. Campaigns, data and payments as one closed loop instead of four vendors stitched together. Every week that loop moves millions of dollars in payments, ingests nearly 100 million rows of client data and serves almost 10 million API requests. About the Product Team The product team is small: two PMs, one designer and a distributed engineering team of about ten. You would be our second product hire. There is no product ops layer, no analyst and no one sitting between you and the client, or between you and the code. The role You will own a set of topics end to end. Not "manage a backlog" in the abstract, but pick up messy input from clients and customer success, turn it into something the team can build, get it shipped, and then make sure it actually gets used. Turn requests into work. Client and CS requests arrive as symptoms, not specs. You dig into what is actually being asked, decide whether it is a bug, a gap, a training problem or a real product need, and write it up so a developer can pick it up without a meeting. Prioritize. You decide what gets built next among a lot of competing, legitimate asks, and you can explain the reasoning to a client, a developer and a founder in three different ways. Firefight. Bugs and urgent client issues will land on you. You triage, reproduce, escalate the real ones, and close the loop with whoever raised it. Discovery. You help figure out what we should build next, from client conversations, usage data and your own read of the market. Data. You are comfortable with data end to end: getting it, questioning it, and deciding what to do about it. Own outcomes, not output. Shipping is the midpoint, not the finish line. If a feature launches and nobody knows it exists or nobody adopts it, that is your problem to solve. You will write the client email, record the walkthrough, check the numbers a month later and tell us honestly whether it worked. Wear multiple hats. Small changes you can do yourself with Claude, you do yourself. Otherwise: specs, debugging, data and dashboards, release notes, client emails, whatever the topic needs. There is no one to hand it to. What this role is not It is not a role where you write requirements and hand them to someone else. It is not a role with a defined scope that stays defined. And it is not a role where you can be effective while waiting to be told what to do. How we work Very little process and very few meetings. No planning ritual that exists to justify the previous planning ritual. If something is not working, we change it the next day. The tradeoff is that nothing will be handed to you. There is no queue of pre-groomed tickets, no one checking whether you did the thing, and no process to hide behind if a topic quietly stalls. Autonomy and accountability come as a pair here. We use Claude heavily across product work: analysis, drafting, prototyping, bulk operations across Linear, Slack, HubSpot and our data.
